Judgment calls: (a) this drafter marks every wire crossover with a sharp downward V-notch in the horizontal; verified at 16x at (117,211), (209,203), (285,197), (363,194) on R2, (117,279), (209,268), (282,277) on R3 and (115,357) on R4 - all eight are crossings, NOT junctions, so C1..C4 pass through the middle rows without connecting. Real connections in this drawing are drawn as plain T's (left edge, right edge, top rail taps, C2/C3/C4 bottom ends), one of which (C2 on R4) even carries a dot. (b) The one genuinely ambiguous point is (480,273), where row R3's ground lead crosses the right edge rail on its way to GND 4. A 30x18 px pixel dump shows a clean 1-px X with no dot and no notch. Read as a CROSSOVER (two nets): the guide's rule is 'plain X with no dot = two nets', and the alternative (junction) would put C3, C4 and C5 all on ground, which short-circuits BOTH I-DC 6 (C3->C4) and V-DC 1 (C4->C5). Two shorted sources out of five is not a credible netlist, so the crossover reading is taken; it yields 7 nets with every net >=2 terminals and no degenerate element. Flagged for human re-check. (c) All 2-terminal parts are listed left-terminal-first as drawn (top-then-bottom for none here); 2-terminal order does not affect any metric. (d) Nothing is off-frame: every bbox centre lies inside 512x512, and no lead runs off the image edge.
